title: Diagnose the Codex proposal invocation-to-elicitation gap

requirement.summary: Determine why the exact AgentGov proposal tool started in the single authorized Codex App Server replay but no native form request was observed before the turn completed.

objective.rationale: The matching trigger now has positive exact-call-start evidence, leaving form elicitation or presentation after invocation as the only observed live-host gap.

goal: Use official Codex App Server documentation, locally generated protocol/schema evidence, Adapter source, deterministic tests, and retained normalized replay evidence to classify the most likely failing layer and identify bounded follow-up options without changing behavior.
non_goals: Do not run another Codex turn, model request, external replay, or form interaction.
Do not infer a human proposal decision, create or admit a proposed task, or implement the replay's inner request.
Do not change Core, Adapter, protocol, schema, configuration, installed runtime, tests, release identity, or architecture.
Do not retain or reconstruct raw replay requests, transcripts, Agent messages, reasoning, tool arguments, unbounded output, credentials, source content, or absolute event paths.
Do not commit, push, publish, release, deploy, merge, or mutate a consumer repository.
acceptance_signals: Official Codex App Server documentation and the local protocol/schema surface are compared for the exact MCP elicitation server-request event and capability negotiation path.
Adapter source and deterministic fixtures establish whether a direct initialized form-capable client reaches elicitation when the proposal tool is invoked with valid normalized input.
The retained normalized replay evidence is interpreted without overstating tool completion, form emission, host presentation, or Adapter failure.
The diagnosis names the most likely failing layer, confidence and residual unknowns, plus bounded follow-up options that remain separately human-controlled.
No new model turn, replay, form response, product behavior change, configuration change, installed-runtime change, or task admission occurs.

items: The retained evidence records a call start and terminal turn but does not retain whether an exact completion carried a recognized success or structured AgentGov error, so the diagnosis must not claim the Adapter completed or failed.
Official App Server documentation may describe the wire contract without documenting every current-client presentation behavior.
A local direct MCP probe could prove Adapter behavior but cannot prove how the Codex Agent or UI handled the same live call.

stop_conditions: Stop before any Codex turn, external replay, native form response, model transmission, product implementation, source/config/install change, or task admission.
Stop if diagnosis requires raw replay reconstruction or evidence outside the documented allow-list.
Stop at bounded uncertainty if official and retained local evidence cannot distinguish Adapter emission from App Server forwarding or UI presentation.
Stop before any Git action, publication, release, deployment, merge, or consumer mutation.

decision.rationale: On 2026-08-09, the bounded diagnosis completed without a model turn or repository behavior change. Official and generated schemas support the request; two valid-input no-model direct calls proved Adapter form generation and App Server parsing through zero-write decline results. The live summary cannot distinguish a structured pre-form error from forwarding or presentation because it omits completion-presence and AgentGov-error evidence. Any normalizer correction, replay, or product fix requires a separate product-owner decision.
